title: Do not require config.assets.compile = true
body: Right now it looks like Marksmith requires `config.assets.compile` to be set to `true` for SVGs that are required. But I would assume lots of Rails apps in production would have this set to `false`. Could be nice if this is not a requirement and svgs can be ejected. Appologies if I missed smth, I just did a quick install based on README to try it out.
author: strzibny

comments.body:
I haven't thought about that.
Yes. That could be the case in some apps.

Do you have experience with setting up ejecting svgs?
Would you be able to send in a PR?

Ok I checked that the gem does produce these assets with a fingerprint and that Rails default is `config.assets.digest = true`. 

So I think it's alright.

It only won't work if we have this:

```
# do not fallback to assets pipeline
config.assets.compile = false

# do not use fingerprinted assets
config.assets.digest = false
```

I am still thinking how could I see the error initially since the default should be working.

Got it!
Yeah, we'll cross that bridge when we get there.
I guess we could export them as static assets in the build step before bundling...

title: Add support for custom icons
body:
Loving this gem! 

I wish I could pull the icons in the toolbar from my own iconset so they match the rest of my site's look and feel. I tried overriding `Marksmith::Helper#marksmith_toolbar_button` but it looks like the one in the engine is used before any helper defined in the Rails app.

I'm not sure how to go about this in an elegant way...maybe a config hash that takes the name of the function (bold, italic) and maps it to a proc, which you can define to pull an image or an SVG or anything else? Now sure how well this plays with the asset pipeline...maybe it could be configured to use a named Rails helper first, if defined, and if not fallback to the existing `image_tag` and included SVG icons?

I did discover that if I copy views/marksmith/shared/_editor.html.erb to my own codebase then I can change anything I want, including the icons! However, this makes it much more difficult to stay in sync with updates from the main gem. ☹️
author: cannikin

comments.body:
I see what you mean @cannikin 
Would extracting that particular area with the icons to a separate partial that you could override make it easier?

I'm not sure if we want to introduce a configuration value and separate DSL just for that at this moment in time.

The changes look awesome @adrianthedev ! We've swapped over to using ActionText though (our editor is gonna be used by normies that don't really grok Markdown) so I haven't actually tested it. 😬 But that direction of making the different areas customizable is definitely the way to go!

That's cool!
What did you end up using? Trix, Rhino, something else?
We implemented Rhino and we're pretty happy with it.
I did Trix, but hadn't heard of Rhino...now that I'm looking I'm very intrigued 👀 Being able to extend it will stuff like tables would be really nice...

title: bug: `ActionMailer` dependency when loading eagerly
body:
When resources are loaded eagerly, `ActionMailer` is being required by Marksmith. The Rails application I'm building does not include `ActionMailer` and therefore it breaks when `config.eager_load = true`

Maybe it's by design, but it requires some hacking around to make it work.

Thank you for the work on this gem (pun intended)!

---

**Error**
```bash
 /Users/elvinas/.local/share/mise/installs/ruby/3.4.1/lib/ruby/gems/3.4.0/gems/marksmith-0.1.2/app/mailers/marksmith/application_mailer.rb:2:in '<module:Marksmith>': uninitialized constant Marksmith::ActionMailer (NameError)                     web    |
   class ApplicationMailer < ActionMailer::Base
                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Did you mean?  ActionCable
```

---

**Workaround**

```ruby
# config/initializers/marksmith.rb

module Marksmith
  class ActionMailer
    class Base; end
  end

  class ApplicationMailer
    def default(**); end
  end
end
```

This is kind of related and inspired by #18
author: elvinaspredkelis

comments.body:
AFAIC it should not be dependent to Action Mailer.

Great catch!
Thanks for reporting. Will remove in the next release.
And thanks for the kind words. I wanted a gem like this since forever and I'm glad that more people like it as much.

title: Undefined method `rails_direct_uploads_url' for an instance of MiniRouter
body:
Showing /Users/yordan/.local/share/mise/installs/ruby/3.3.6/lib/ruby/gems/3.3.0/gems/marksmith-0.1.2/app/views/marksmith/shared/_editor.html.erb where line #19 raised:

undefined method `rails_direct_uploads_url' for an instance of MiniRouter

I'm getting the above error when trying to use `<%= f.marksmith :long_description %>`.

Sounds like a bug to me.
author: yorsant

comments.body:
Hey @yorsant, as far as I understand, by default, Marksmith requires ActiveStorage installed in the application for things to work, that's where the missing URL helper is coming from.

Even though you can pass `upload_url` as an argument to the form helper:

```erb
<%# app/views/marksmith/shared/_editor.html.erb %>
upload_url = if local_assigns[:upload_url].present?
  local_assigns[:upload_url]
elsif defined?(ActiveStorage)
  main_app.rails_direct_uploads_url
end
```

As far as I can tell, Active Storage is hardcoded in the `#pathFromBlob` method of the Marksmith Stimulus controller because it uses the Active Storage route prefix to generate the link that ends up inserting into the editor:

```javascript
// app/frontend/controllers/marksmith_controller.js
#pathFromBlob(blob) {
  return `/rails/active_storage/blobs/redirect/${blob.signed_id}/${blob.filename}` 
}
```

I hope this helps.

Hey @yorsant. 

I wonder what kind of setup you have there. 
I see a mention about a MiniRouter. 
Also, as @erozas mentioned, it's still pretty tied up to ActiveStorage, so you should have that installed in your app and then it should work. 
We plan to make the upload feature  more agnostic in the future. 

Until then, please check out the configuration guide on how to disable the uploads and you'll be able to use it as a markdown editor.
